title: Escarpment and Current
premise: Hazel Delacroix, a salvage diver on the Gulf coast, is hired to recover equipment from a wreck the navy refuses to explain, and finds among the salvage a concession map pointing upriver to an expedition that has gone silent. When the expedition's financier hires him to run supplies through the closing monsoon window, Hazel discovers the missing team alive but fractured — one of them, surveyor Ines Okonkwo, has uncovered that the concession's true prize is not timber or minerals but a drowned colonial archive worth killing for. As permits expire and the river rises, Hazel and Ines must choose between salvaging their own survival and exposing the corruption that bought the expedition. The story ends with Hazel surrendering the recovered archive to federal investigators at the cost of his boat and livelihood, walking away from the water with nothing but his life and Ines's testimony.
about_author: H. M. Villalobos is the pen name of a former marine surveyor who spent a decade working coastal salvage contracts across the Gulf of Mexico and Central America. They now write adventure fiction from a houseboat, drawing on firsthand knowledge of rivers, wrecks, and the people who make their living from both.

chapters.title: The Wreck Nobody Names
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Diving a charted-as-empty wreck site, Hazel recovers a sealed case stamped with a concession number and finds navy patrol boats shadowing his barge. He pockets the case rather than declare it. Emotional beat: wary competence curdling into unease as he realizes the job was never about salvage.

chapters.title: Concession 44
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Deciphering the case's contents — permits, a river map, and a radio log ending mid-sentence — Hazel traces them to the Delgado expedition, silent for six weeks. A lawyer named Brandt offers triple pay to run supplies upriver before monsoon. Beat: greed wrestling with instinct; he takes the contract.

chapters.title: Leaking Hull
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Provisioning his aging boat, the Marisol, Hazel discovers hull damage the yard won't fix in time and negotiates with a rival diver for parts, learning someone else asked about Concession 44 first. Beat: mounting pressure against the calendar; the river season is closing.

chapters.title: Upstream
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The ascent begins — fuel caches, hostile checkpoints, and a passenger he didn't expect: Ines Okonkwo, the expedition's surveyor, who walked out of the jungle alone and says the others are alive. Beat: distrust between strangers bound by necessity.

chapters.title: What Ines Saw
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Flashback chapter: Ines recounts finding the drowned archive vault beneath the concession's old trading post, and how expedition leader Marcus Vane changed overnight — sealing the site, cutting radios, arming men. Beat: dread; the expedition was never lost, it was captured.

chapters.title: First Contact
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Approaching the base camp, the Marisol takes sniper fire; Hazel grounds her in the shallows and he and Ines go overland, watching Vane's men load crates toward the vault. Beat: fear sharpening into resolve; no turning back now.

chapters.title: The Trading Post
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Ines leads Hazel through flooded tunnels to the archive's edge, revealing documents proving Brandt's firm forged the concession and buried deaths to keep it. Beat: revelation — the price of survival here is complicity, and Ines refused to pay it once already.

chapters.title: Monsoon Breaks
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The rains arrive early, flooding the tunnels and trapping them inside as Vane's men search above. Hazel dives a submerged passage to reach the river side, nearly drowning. Beat: terror and endurance; the wilderness forgives nothing.

chapters.title: Prisoners of the Camp
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Captured at the perimeter, they're held at camp where Ines confronts former colleagues who chose Vane's payroll over the truth. One, engineer Tomas Reyes, quietly slips her a key. Beat: betrayal and fragile alliance; loyalty has a market price.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Vane offers Hazel a share to dive the vault's final chamber — the only one who can. Hazel sees the fortune that would rebuild his life, and the bodies it would be built on. Beat: temptation at its most seductive; power corrupting by invitation.

chapters.title: The Dive
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Underwater in the black flooded chamber, Hazel recovers the archive's core cache but palms a single document instead of handing over everything, gambling Vane won't notice. Beat: cold clarity; he chooses a side without announcing it.

chapters.title: Tomas's Price
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Tomas's aid is exposed; Vane executes him at the riverbank as a lesson. Ines understands the escape must happen now or never. Beat: grief weaponized into urgency; the cost of survival made flesh.

chapters.title: Night Crossing
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. With the key and the hidden document, Hazel and Ines steal a workboat during the storm's worst hours, running Vane's checkpoint gauntlet downriver. Beat: desperate momentum; luck spending itself fast.

chapters.title: Grounded
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. The stolen boat fails in rapids; they lose the supplies but save the archive, hauling it ashore miles from anywhere with Vane's boats behind them. Beat: rock bottom — stripped to skill, stamina, and each other.

chapters.title: The Long Walk
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Overland through concession territory, Ines reveals she once worked for Brandt's firm and helped bury the evidence she now carries. Hazel's trust fractures. Beat: confession and rupture; inheritance of guilt passed down like the archive itself.

chapters.title: River People
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Sheltering with river families who've fought the concession for generations, Hazel learns the archive names their stolen land — and that Brandt's men are buying witnesses along every bend. Beat: solidarity; the fight is bigger than two fugitives.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Bend
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Vane's lead hunter corners them at a ferry crossing; Hazel uses diving knowledge to collapse a submerged mooring and sink the pursuit boat, taking a knife wound doing it. Beat: violent climax of pursuit; survival purchased with blood.

chapters.title: Permits Expire
chapters.summary: POV Ines. At the coastal registry, they learn Brandt has filed to transfer the concession legally within days — the paper trail will erase everything unless the archive reaches federal investigators before signature. Beat: ticking clock reborn; bureaucracy as battlefield.

chapters.title: Brandt's Table
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Hazel walks into Brandt's office offering to sell the archive back — a bluff to force confirmation of the forged permits while Ines copies the registry records. Beat: nerve over firepower; the con is the climax's opening move.

chapters.title: Everything the River Holds
chapters.summary: POV Hazel and Ines alternating. The bluff collapses; Vane arrives, Brandt turns on him, and in the chaos Hazel and Ines escape with the archive intact as investigators — tipped by the river families — raid the offices. Beat: climax; corruption devouring itself.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: POV Ines. Weeks later, Ines testifies; the concession is voided and the river families' claims move forward. Hazel declines reward money, his boat condemned, his trade blacklisted by the firms that feared him. Beat: bittersweet justice; the price of survival finally paid in full.

chapters.title: Escarpment and Current
chapters.summary: POV Hazel. Standing on the escarpment above the river mouth, Hazel watches the current carry the last monsoon out to sea. Ines offers him a place on a legitimate survey crew. He says yes. Beat: quiet resolution — what survives is not what he salvaged, but what he refused to sell.
